about.title: Placentia Car Accident Claims

LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured people in Placentia with an independent personal injury attorney who can review your situation. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Reaching out costs you nothing and starts the process of protecting your options while the details are still fresh.

whyChoose.title: What to Keep in Mind After a Placentia Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but if a government entity (like the city or county) was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault may reduce the final amount. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: Avoid Giving a Recorded Statement to the Other Insurer
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement early, hoping to lock in details before you understand the full extent of your injuries. You're not obligated to give one, and speaking with an attorney first can protect you from statements used against you later.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Placentia?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or a hazard on public property, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's best not to wait to find out which timeline applies to you.

items.question: What if the crash happened near SR-57 or Orangethorpe Avenue?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors like SR-57 and Orangethorpe Avenue see a large share of Placentia's reported injury collisions, which can mean more witnesses, traffic camera footage, or CHP reports available as evidence. An independent attorney can help track down and preserve that kind of documentation before it disappears.

items.question: Will I still be paid if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash, though your recovery amount may be reduced based on your percentage of fault. This is exactly the kind of issue an attorney can help evaluate on your behalf.
